msg: Ultra on root: The tm_dot_prod loop processes 512 int8 elements in 8-element chunks. Each iteration executes 16 byte loads (lb, 5 cycles each), 8 multiplications (mul, 5-6 cycles), 7 additions (add, 3 cycles), and loop overhead. At 4096 iterations, this dominates 95.7% of cycles. The critical path is the 8 independent multiply-accumulate operations per iteration, requiring 41+ cycles for arithmetic alone. Memory loads are also costly but cannot be eliminated by custom ALU instructions.

proposal.title: 4-way int8 dot product with sum reduction
proposal.rationale: Replaces 4 mul (20-24 cycles) + 3 add (9 cycles) = 29-33 cycles with 1 custom instruction (7 cycles). Uses 4 DSP blocks (4x 8x8 signed multipliers) and a 3-input adder tree. Software packs 4 int8s per register via lw (1 load vs 4 lb), then calls dot4_sum twice per 8-element chunk, adding the two results. Saves ~22 cycles per 4 elements, ~44 cycles per loop iteration.

proposal.title: 4-way int8 dot product returning packed 16-bit partials
proposal.rationale: Returns two 16-bit products packed in 32 bits (p0|p1<<16). Requires 2 DSP blocks. Software calls twice for 4 elements, then uses hadd16 (next proposal) to sum pairs. Saves mul latency but adds horizontal add overhead. Less area than dot4_sum but more instructions. Good if area budget tight.

proposal.title: Horizontal add of two 16-bit halves
proposal.rationale: Sums two 16-bit values in one register. Single 16-bit adder, negligible area. Replaces 1 add (3 cycles) with 1 custom (5 cycles) but enables dot4_partials workflow. Actually slower alone, but combined with dot4_partials avoids 32-bit add latency? No, 32-bit add is 3 cycles. This is for pairing with dot4_partials to sum 16-bit partials without sign-extend overhead. Saves 1 cycle vs sign-extend+add.

proposal.title: 4-way int8 multiply-accumulate into 32-bit sum
proposal.rationale: Invalid - no accumulator input. Replaced with byte packing instruction.

proposal.title: Pack 4 bytes from two registers into one 32-bit word
proposal.rationale: Packing instructions don't reduce arithmetic cycles. Loads remain bottleneck. Focus on arithmetic fusion.

proposal.title: 2-way int16 dot product (for requantization)
proposal.rationale: Requantization (0.94% cycles) uses 16-bit multiplies. This fuses 2 mul+1 add (13 cycles) into 1 custom (6 cycles, 2 DSP blocks). Minor overall speedup but uses different data width, covering distinct idea. Area: 2 DSP + adder.

proposal.title: 2-way int8 multiply-accumulate
proposal.rationale: The remainder loop processes 1-7 elements with scalar multiply-add (3-5 cycles each). mula2_8_acc handles 2 elements in one 5-7 cycle instruction, replacing 2-4 scalar instructions (6-10 cycles) and their adds. Saves ~2-4 cycles per 2 remainder elements; remainder is ~12.5% of dot-product work.

proposal.title: 16x16 multiply with 16-bit right shift
proposal.rationale: Requantization (2.75% of cycles) typically computes (sum * scale) >> shift. A 16x16 multiply takes 5-6 cycles (MUL) plus shift (3 cycles) = 8-9 cycles. This instruction fuses them into 5-7 cycles, saving 2-3 cycles per output channel (64 channels).

proposal.title: 4-way int8 multiply-accumulate with add of rs1
proposal.rationale: Fuses the mula4.acc (5-7 cycles) and the following 32-bit add (3 cycles) into one 5-7 cycle instruction, saving 3 cycles per 4-element chunk. The main loop does two 4-element chunks per 8 elements (4096 iterations), saving 3*2*4096 = 24,576 cycles (~9.5% of baseline). Requires software to keep running sum in rs1 and data in rs2 (or vice versa), which is feasible by holding sum in a register across the loop.

proposal.title: 2-way int8 multiply-accumulate with add of rs1
proposal.rationale: Packs two int8 A in rs1[15:0], two int8 B in rs2[15:0], and the 16-bit running sum in rs1[31:16]. Returns updated 16-bit sum (low 16 bits) plus dot product. Fuses 2-element dot (5-7 cycles) and add (3 cycles) into one instruction, saving 3 cycles per 2 elements. For the main loop, we can process 8 elements as four 2-element chunks: 4 instructions replace 2 mula4.acc + 2 adds (2*5-7 + 2*3 = 16-20 cycles) with 4*5-7 = 20-28 cycles — similar or slightly worse. But it enables the remainder loop to fuse add, and if sum fits 16 bits (often true for int8 dot products of length 512: max 512*127*127 ~ 8M < 2^23), we can keep sum in 16 bits for a while. Main benefit is code density and remainder handling.

proposal.title: 4-way int8 dot-product plus 32-bit accumulate
proposal.rationale: Fuses the 5-7 cycle dot4_sum and the 3-cycle ADD into one 5-7 cycle instruction, saving 3 cycles/iteration. Loop body drops from 7 to 6 instructions (removes explicit ADD). Estimated 24k cycles saved (7.5% total). Area: ~4 DSP blocks + adder (~2.5% LUTs).
